exact_weight_and_quantifiers.literal_profile: P(Z,rho,u)=chi(u/Z)*F(u)*exp(2*pi*I*rho*u), chi=CommonSmoothCutoff.poissonSmoothLowPass, F=Fourier(CommonSmoothCutoff.dyadicCutoffSchwartz). Source uses fourier(1:Z) on UnitAddCircle and its sign is positive.
exact_weight_and_quantifiers.fixed_data: Fix d>=1, q_i:R->C smooth compactly supported, Q(t)=product_i q_i(t_i), fixed real vectors a,b,c in R^d, and K=product_i tsupport(q_i). All constants may depend on these fixed objects and the derivative order, never on the atom/scales below. Use EuclideanSpace R (Fin d) for native inner-product Fourier APIs; an unadorned Pi type has the wrong default norm for this interface.
exact_weight_and_quantifiers.varying_data: For every Z>=1, signed u0,rho0 in R, and R>=0 such that |rho0*exp(b dot t)|<=R for every t in K, define u(t)=u0*exp(a dot t), rho(t)=rho0*exp(b dot t), W(t)=Q(t)*exp(c dot t)*P(Z,rho(t),u(t)). An optional actual scalar prefactor A0 must be factored out; its cost is |A0| and cannot be hidden in C.
exact_weight_and_quantifiers.mixed_bound: For every J:N there exists C_J>0 such that simultaneously for every coordinate word ell of length j<=J and all varying data above, all t satisfy |D_ell W(t)|<=C_J*(1+R)^j. Here D_[]W=W and D_(i::ell)W(t)=fderiv R (D_ell W) t (e_i). The bound includes all mixed rho effects and implies the multi-index version. W and every derivative have support in K.
exact_weight_and_quantifiers.L1_and_identity: There exists C_L1>0 depending only on fixed data such that integral_R^d |Fourier W(xi)| dxi <= C_L1*(1+R)^(2d), and W(t)=integral_R^d Fourier W(xi)*product_i exp(2*pi*I*xi_i*t_i) dxi, absolutely. At positive x_i with t_i=log(x_i/x_i0), the factors are separate imaginary powers of x_i/x_i0. This is joint Fourier inversion in log coordinates; no Mellin-inversion supplier is assumed.
exact_weight_and_quantifiers.zero_and_signs: Abstract u0 and rho0 may be zero or signed and the derivative theorem remains true. Application to h uses h>0 and h<0 separately; log|h| is never applied to h=0. Actual poissonNonzeroFrequency has a separate zero branch at h=0, whereas P(Z,rho,0) need not vanish.

complete_mixed_derivative_argument: Set x=u/Z, y=u, v=rho*u, and G(x,y,v)=chi(x)*F(y)*exp(2*pi*I*v). With Z fixed, differentiation in t_i on the pullback is exactly a_i E_x+a_i E_y+(a_i+b_i) E_v, with E_z=z*d/dz. This identity includes the rho derivative; treating rho as fixed in a full-label derivative would incorrectly replace a_i+b_i by a_i.

For Q*exp(c dot t)*G, D_i acts as derivative on Q plus c_i plus the above three commuting Euler operators. Repeated Leibniz expansion of a coordinate word of length j yields finitely many terms (D^nu Q)*exp(c dot t)*E_x^k chi(x)*E_y^l F(y)*E_v^m exp(2*pi*I*v), with |nu|+k+l+m<=j and coefficients depending only on fixed a,b,c and j. Constants from differentiating the exponential prefactor count in j but introduce no varying scale.

For any smooth f, E_z^k f=sum_{s=0}^k S(k,s) z^s f^(s)(z), including k=0. The finite coefficients satisfy the ordinary Stirling recurrence, so an implementation may prove this by induction without importing a Stirling API. For chi, every derivative is supported in [-2,2]; hence |x^s chi^(s)(x)|<=2^s sup|chi^(s)|, a fixed finite constant. This pays cutoff derivatives without a positive Z power. In fact this log argument works for every Z>0, although the requested lemma retains Z>=1.

E_y^l F(y)=sum_{s<=l} S(l,s)y^s F^(s)(y). E_v^m exp(2*pi*I*v)=exp(2*pi*I*v)*sum_{k<=m} S(m,k)(2*pi*I*v)^k. Its norm is bounded by the corresponding finite sum of (2*pi)^k*|rho|^k*|u|^k. The phase has modulus one for signed rho,u. No bound on |u0| is used.

In each combined term, |u|^(s+k)*|F^(s)(u)| is uniformly bounded by a fixed Schwartz seminorm with weight s+k<=l+m<=j and derivative s<=j. In particular one common bound B_J=2^J*sup_{(r,n)<= (J,J)} seminorm_R(r,n)(F) suffices. On K, |rho|^k<=(1+R)^j. Derivatives of Q and exp(c dot t) are uniformly bounded on fixed compact K; outside K all D^nu Q vanish. Thus summing the finite expansion proves C_J*(1+R)^j, uniformly in Z,u0,rho0. This is an explicit mixed-parameter proof, not an invocation of the ordinary-u candidate theorem.

Smoothness of W follows from the literal smooth cutoff, fixed Schwartz F, real exponentials, linear forms, and Complex.exp. Its support is contained in K. HasCompactSupport.toSchwartzMap then bundles this actual W as a Schwartz map; Fourier W is Schwartz and integrable by native APIs. No arbitrary unknown function or target estimate is supplied as a premise.

joint_fourier_L1_cost.normalization: Native Fourier is hat W(xi)=integral exp(-2*pi*I<t,xi>)*W(t) dt; inverse uses +2*pi and no extra scalar. All measures here are ordinary coordinate Lebesgue measure in EuclideanSpace with the standard orthonormal basis.
joint_fourier_L1_cost.operator: Let T_i=Id-D_i^2 and T=product_{i=1}^d T_i. Repeated native fourier_lineDerivOp_eq yields Fourier(TW)(xi)=product_i(1+4*pi^2*xi_i^2)*hat W(xi). T expands into the 2^d mixed derivatives D^(2*1_S) for S subset Fin d, with signs (-1)^|S|. Its maximum total derivative order is exactly2d, with order at most2 in each coordinate.
joint_fourier_L1_cost.integrated: The exact one-dimensional integral of (1+4*pi^2*x^2)^(-1) is1/2, by y=2*pi*x and integral(1+y^2)^(-1)=pi. Fubini/Tonelli therefore gives ||hat W||_L1 <=2^(-d)*sum_S ||D^(2*1_S)W||_L1 <=2^(-d)*vol(K)*sum_S C_(2|S|)*(1+R)^(2|S|) <=C_L1*(1+R)^(2d). A fixed enclosing box may replace K to avoid zero-volume bookkeeping. No independent one-variable transform bounds are incorrectly multiplied for a non-product W.
joint_fourier_L1_cost.Mellin_tau_convention: If G(tau)=integral W(t)*exp(-I*tau dot t) dt, then G(tau)=hat W(tau/(2*pi)). Inversion is (2*pi)^(-d)*integral G(tau)*exp(I*tau dot t) dtau. The effective absolute separation cost is (2*pi)^(-d)*integral|G|=integral|hat W|. Omitting this factor would change the normalization.
joint_fourier_L1_cost.prefactors: For actual A0*W, both pointwise derivatives and transform L1 gain |A0|. Normalized monomial exp(c dot t) is harmless on fixed support; arbitrary actual V/L is not uniformly bounded by a fixed constant and is retained explicitly.

Its private status must be respected when implementing a reusable bridge.

original_kappa_budget.Gram_or_square: If a spectral operator norm is bounded after integrating one separated kernel and the resulting bound is squared, the L1 norm squares. Likewise independently separating two row copies yields the product of their L1 norms. Therefore d=2 can cost8kappa<=0.08sigma; d=7 can cost28kappa<=0.28sigma. original_kappa_budget.precise_open_issue: There is no proved spectral endpoint in this audit specifying whether the actual cost enters before/after Cauchy, square root, packet summation or root-operator losses. No new smaller-kappa assumption and no hidden target-estimate wrapper is introduced.
